## Vocabulary

- **self**: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs (17/3)

## Definitions

- [statement] Swap V2 /order is a meta-aggregator. Metis (Jupiter's onchain multi-hop, multi-split router), JupiterZ (off-chain RFQ market makers), Dflow and OKX all quote, and the best execution price wins. /build uses Metis only. Jupiter says RFQ quotes often beat onchain routing by 5 to 20 bps on major pairs but publishes no data for that range. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md

## How it works

- [statement] Jupiter says its routing sidelines or penalizes sources that underdeliver: the routing docs describe a self-learning mechanism that sidelines underperforming sources, and trade press on Metis V8 reports slippage penalties on venues with poor realized execution plus just-in-time onchain split selection. Neither source gives before/after execution data. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://solanafloor.com/news/jupiter-unveils-metis-v8-router-promising-to-solve-quote-execution-drift
- [statement] On a dynamic-fee pool the fee a quote returns can change between block N and block N+1 even if reserves have not moved, because every swap shifts the volatility accumulator; Raydium says a quote can be off by a few bps if a reactive pool is hit between quote and execution, and that the accumulator and last-update timestamp are public on-chain so clients can replicate the formula. Meteora's design behaves the same way: the accumulator rises with bin movement and decays with elapsed time. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.raydium.io/products/clmm/fees · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://docs.meteora.ag/core-products/dlmm/formulas
- [statement] On /order, the top-level feeBps field is the total fee rate and platformFee.feeBps is Jupiter's platform fee alone. The two differ when a gasless surcharge applies. feeMint names the token the fee is taken in, chosen from a priority list: SOL, stablecoins, liquid staking tokens, bluechips, others. After /execute, the fee equals totalInputAmount minus inputAmountResult when feeMint is the input mint, or outputAmountResult minus totalOutputAmount when it is the output mint. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/gasless.md, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/ultra/fees
- [statement] The /build (Router) path charges no Jupiter swap fee and routes through Metis only. An integrator can add its own fee with platformFeeBps and a feeAccount, which can be any SPL token account it controls. /build uses a fixed 50 bps slippage by default and switches to RTSE only when the caller passes slippageBps=rtse. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/build · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/slippage.md
- [statement] Gasless swaps cost extra through the swap fee. When the taker holds under 0.01 SOL and the trade is about $10 or more (the minimum is dynamic), Jupiter's sponsor wallet pays gas and rent, and the swap fee rises by the USD value of that SOL, converted into the traded token. The surcharge is a fixed amount, so small trades pay proportionally more. The docs' example is a 5 bps platform fee plus 7 bps of gasless recoup, shown as feeBps 12. Automatic sponsorship does not fire when referral parameters are set. When JupiterZ wins the route, the market maker pays network and priority fees at no extra charge. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/gasless.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md, https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/swap/fees.md, https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/spot/ultra-mode.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Raydium separates price impact from slippage and tolerance. Price impact, impact = (p_before - p_after) / p_before, is a deterministic property of a trade against a specific pool state and can be computed before submission (about 2 x amount_in / reserve_in for small constant-product trades; piecewise on CLMM pools). Realized slippage is (quoted_out - actual_out) / quoted_out. Tolerance is a buffer around the impact: minAmountOut = amountOut x (1 - tolerance), so a 2% impact with 0.5% tolerance puts the floor about 2.5% below pre-trade spot. (low confidence) — https://docs.raydium.io/algorithms/slippage-and-price-impact · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs
- [statement] A referral (integrator) fee on /order ranges from 50 to 255 bps. Jupiter keeps 20% of it and adds no separate platform fee while a referral is active. The integrator must first create a referral account and a referral token account for each fee mint. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/ultra/fees, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing
- [statement] A Token-2022 transfer fee stacks on top of the pool fee. Raydium's worked example turns a nominal 0.25% pool fee into about 1.74% effective when the input token carries a 1% transfer fee and the output token 0.5% (1 - 0.99 x 0.9975 x 0.995). Raydium tells integrators to quote such pools with the SDK's getComputeAmountOut. (low confidence) — https://docs.raydium.io/reference/fee-comparison.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Swap V2 has two paths. /order is a meta-aggregator where Metis (onchain multi-hop, multi-split), JupiterZ (off-chain RFQ market makers) and the third-party routers Dflow and OKX all compete and the best execution price wins. /build uses Metis only. JupiterZ transactions cannot be modified after return, so CPI or custom-instruction use cases must use /build. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs
- [statement] Swap V2 /order quotes include a price impact value, but the routing docs give no calculation method or thresholds, so callers cannot audit it from the docs alone. (low confidence) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs
- [statement] Slippage tolerance is a floor on output chosen at order time, not a forecast of cost. On /order, RTSE sets it from token category, recent slippage data and live failure rates and embeds it in the transaction, and a fixed slippageBps overrides RTSE. Jupiter's user docs warn that a high tolerance in manual mode can give unfavorable execution prices and a low one can make transactions fail. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/advanced/slippage.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/swap/fees.md, https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/spot/ultra-mode.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Gasless swaps cost extra. When the taker holds under 0.01 SOL and Jupiter fronts the SOL, it raises the swap fee by the USD value of the SOL it pays, converted into the traded token, on top of the normal swap fee. The extra is a fixed amount rather than a percentage, so small trades pay proportionally more; Jupiter says gasless is offered only when the recovered gas is within 10% of the trade (about a $10 minimum). In Swap V2 the extra shows in top-level feeBps but not in platformFee.feeBps (documented example: 5 bps platform plus 7 bps gasless gives feeBps 12). JupiterZ RFQ routes are gasless at no added cost because the market maker pays the fees. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/swap/fees.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md, https://developers.jup.ag/blog/ultra-v3
- [statement] Migrating from Swap API V1 changes fee data: V2 route plans report bps instead of percent, and V2 instructions no longer emit fee events, so fee-accounting code written for V1 must change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/routing · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] If the integrator has not created a referral token account for the fee mint, the Swap V2 order still returns and the user still swaps, but the integrator fee is silently not collected; check feeBps and platformFee.feeBps in the response. (low confidence) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs
- [statement] If the referral token account for the order's feeMint does not exist, /order still returns and the swap still executes, but the integrator's fee is not collected. The response can then fall back to the default platform fee, so check feeBps and platformFee.feeBps after wiring a referral. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs
- [statement] A quote goes stale fast. Aggregator routes (Metis, Dflow, OKX) stay valid until lastValidBlockHeight and RFQ routes until expireAt, but prices can still move against the user inside that window. Jupiter's guidance is to sign and submit as soon as the order arrives. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/swap/v2/fees.md · keywords: DEX swap fees slippage and Jupiter routing costs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/blog/why-you-dont-get-what-you-were-quoted
